forecast.statement: Six-month base case: gold around USD 3,900–4,700/oz, with substantial risk outside that range.
forecast.resolution_criteria: Use the last published LBMA Gold Price PM in USD per troy ounce on or before 2027-03-28. Bear: below 3900; base: at least 3900 and below 4700; bull: at least 4700. Do not substitute intraday spot or futures without documenting a benchmark change.

forecast.synthesis: Traverse conflict → shipping → energy → policy → real yields/currency → gold. Compare that headwind with central-bank and investor demand. The direct safe-haven channel can oppose the inflation/rate channel, so avoid the simplistic rule that war always raises gold. Count yield-to-gold and yield-to-investor-flow effects as related paths. The forecast branch weights are the external agent’s subjective synthesis, not a mechanical multiplication of edge weights.
forecast.base_rate: No empirical six-month conditional gold return distribution was fitted. Observed monthly volatility motivates broad scenarios but is not a calibrated base rate.
assumptions: The USD/LBMA resolution benchmark remains available.
No mechanical price floor is implied by central-bank buying.
The direction and strength of causal links are qualitative hypotheses, not estimated coefficients.
red_team: War-driven energy inflation can hurt gold through tighter policy even while safe-haven demand rises.
Official buying and investor inflows may already be reflected in price and can reverse.
A liquidity shock could force gold sales; the graph omits detailed leverage and supply responses.
uncertainties: Probabilities are uncalibrated agent judgments; confidence is subjective.
Official-sector and ETF data have reporting lags; the selected evidence is not exhaustive.
Diplomatic outcomes, future real yields, and FX responses remain uncertain.
